boards.school_name: The University of Texas at Dallas
boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented UT Dallas traditions, from the comet salute to the reflecting-pool ring ceremony.

cards.title: Make the Whoosh
cards.subtitle: UT Dallas comet salute
cards.notes: Learn the arm-and-hand comet salute, then use it when joining campus spirit moments and photos.
cards.short_summary: A UT Dallas unity salute named for a comet’s imagined sound.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Dallas says the Whoosh was invented in the early 1990s as a way for students to show campus unity.
cards.access_notes: A gesture rather than a venue; learn it through UT Dallas orientation and spirit programming.

cards.title: Dunk a Class Ring
cards.subtitle: Spring and fall reflecting-pool ceremony
cards.notes: If you have a UT Dallas class ring, check ceremony announcements and bring it for the reflecting-pool ritual.
cards.short_summary: A ceremony where eligible students dunk class rings in campus reflecting pools.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Dallas states that undergraduate and graduate students are invited to dunk class rings in campus reflecting pools each spring and fall.
cards.access_notes: Participation requires a class ring; verify the current ceremony date and eligibility with UT Dallas.

cards.title: Play Oozeball
cards.subtitle: Annual mud volleyball tournament
cards.notes: Form a six-to-ten-person team and follow Student Ambassadors registration guidance for the mud-volleyball tournament.
cards.short_summary: UT Dallas’ annual mud volleyball event began in 2002.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Dallas identifies Oozeball as an annual mud volleyball tournament organized by Student Ambassadors, with teams of six to ten players.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current registration, weather guidance, accessibility, and event rules before participating.

cards.entity_name: Rubbing Cecil Green’s Head for Luck
cards.title: Visit Cecil Green Before Finals
cards.subtitle: Cecil H. Green Hall west entrance
cards.notes: Find the Cecil H. Green sculpture near Green Hall’s west entrance and observe the finals-week good-luck custom.
cards.short_summary: Students use a founder’s sculpture as a finals-week luck ritual.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Dallas reports that many students rub founder Cecil H. Green’s sculpture head for good luck during finals week.
cards.access_notes: The effigy is located near the west entrance of Cecil H. Green Hall, according to UT Dallas.

cards.title: Meet Temoc
cards.subtitle: UT Dallas mascot
cards.notes: Spot the blue-skinned comet mascot at campus spirit events and learn the name’s playful comet connection.
cards.short_summary: Temoc is UT Dallas’ comet-in-human-form mascot.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Dallas identifies Temoc as its official mascot, designed by student Aaron Aryanpur and adopted in April 1998.
cards.access_notes: Mascot appearances vary by event; consult current UT Dallas event listings for scheduled appearances.

cards.title: Learn the Fight Song
cards.subtitle: Ends with the Whoosh
cards.notes: Use the official lyrics and recording to learn the chorus, then add the Whoosh at the song’s close.
cards.short_summary: UT Dallas’ fight song uses the musical arrangement of “Tiger Rag.”
cards.evidence_claim: UT Dallas says its fight song follows the musical arrangement of “Tiger Rag” and prints the lyrics ending with “Whoosh!”
cards.access_notes: The official traditions page provides the lyrics and a downloadable audio recording.

cards.title: Sing the Alma Mater
cards.subtitle: University song by Rodriguez, Dunn and Reynolds
cards.notes: Read the official lyrics before a campus ceremony or spirit event so you can recognize the university song.
cards.short_summary: The alma mater pairs music by Robert Xavier Rodriguez with lyrics by Bill Dunn and Neely Reynolds.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Dallas credits Robert Xavier Rodriguez with the alma mater’s music and Bill Dunn and Neely Reynolds with its lyrics.
cards.access_notes: The official traditions page publishes the alma mater lyrics.

cards.title: Spot the Ceremonial Mace
cards.subtitle: Processional symbol
cards.notes: Watch for the handcrafted mace at a university procession and look closely for its Treaty Oak, microchip and spaceflight details.
cards.short_summary: A processional mace connecting UT Dallas’ founding story, science and Texas history.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Dallas says the ceremonial mace leads processions and incorporates Treaty Oak wood, Texas Instruments microchips, and material flown on Space Shuttle Endeavour.
cards.access_notes: It is carried during various university events; visibility depends on the ceremony program.

cards.title: Join International Week
cards.subtitle: Annual spring cultural celebration
cards.notes: Check the iWeek schedule for student-led events, performances and cultural activities across the campus community.
cards.short_summary: A spring tradition highlighting UT Dallas’ global community.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Dallas describes International Week as an annual tradition featuring student-led and campus-partner events that highlight the campus’s global impact.
cards.access_notes: UT Dallas says planning is underway for iWeek 2027; check the official site for announced details.

cards.title: Walk Legacy Lane
cards.subtitle: Behind McDermott Library
cards.notes: Walk the tree-lined creekside path behind McDermott Library and read engraved pavers organized by class year.
cards.short_summary: A paved alumni legacy path marked by personalized stones.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Dallas describes Legacy Lane as a tree-lined path behind McDermott Library with personalized engraved paving stones organized by class year.
cards.access_notes: The path is behind McDermott Library; access should follow current campus access rules.
